question:
Which of the following is known as the Paper tax in India?

I. Wealth tax

II. Goods and services tax
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Wealth tax** was a direct tax levied on the net wealth of individuals, Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs), and companies in India. It was abolished in the **Union Budget 2015-16** due to its low revenue collection and high administrative costs.
 
• The term "Paper tax" refers to **Wealth tax** as it requires detailed documentation and paperwork related to the assets owned by the taxpayer. *Hence, statement I is correct.*
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**, introduced in **July 2017**, is an indirect tax system that subsumes multiple indirect taxes. It is not referred to as "Paper tax" as it is based on consumption rather than wealth documentation. *Hence, statement II is not correct.*
